- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.5) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply smoothing filter to dampen 3–5 day peaks.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.75), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of past 30 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates downward trends after strong bullish sentiment; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.3.  
- If sentiment shows strong momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive days >0.75), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile or erratic (alternating +/–), model overfits short-term noise; use 10-day rolling average to filter out false signals.
